messages:
ashley (acct-exec): Urgent POC blocker from a prospect. Their app intermittently fails JSON.parse when using our function-calling + json_mode (non-streaming). They receive extra trailing bytes after the JSON. Can we triage?

sam (sales-engineer): Can you paste the raw HTTP response (headers + body) and confirm if they reuse connections or do retries?

ashley (acct-exec): They pasted this snippet (copied literally):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "choices": [{"message": {"name": "create_item", "arguments": "{\"id\": \"abc\"}"}}]
}
--trailing--

They said model=redwood-medium-v1, streaming=false, keep-alive=true, and they do client retries on 429/5xx. Also saw a 429 with X-Request-Id: req_zz101.

tyler (ml-eng): Short analysis: if the client retries on the same TCP connection while our worker is still finishing the previous response, leftover bytes can get concatenated. Need the full request ids and the customer's raw request (curl or SDK call) to reproduce serializer path.

prashant (infra): Ops-bot, pull traces for req_zz101 and nearby ids. Also note: if this is due to client double-encoding the arguments string, we need the sent request body.

ops-bot: Trace found: req_zz101 -> worker-5. Related span req_zz102. Worker log at 2026-03-25T12:34:10Z includes WARN "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes".

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN is the smoking gun for trailing bytes. Short-term mitigations to give the customer: 1) add a defensive sanitizer that extracts the first top-level JSON before JSON.parse, 2) enable SDK idempotency / disable aggressive client retries, 3) optionally switch to streaming=true and parse as a stream.

sam (sales-engineer): They also asked: if they remove client retries, will that change POC costs? Need a concise answer.

prashant (infra): One-liner: aggressive retries can increase token spend roughly proportional to the retry rate (e.g., 10% retry rate could yield ~10% extra tokens). Using SDK de-dup or idempotency keys avoids duplicate charges.

tyler (ml-eng): Engineering plan: add a small shim to append a canonical delimiter when json_mode=true so concatenation is detectable by clients, add unit/integration tests simulating keep-alive + retry, and investigate if any server-side double-serialization occurs. Estimated: shim patch + tests 2-3h, staging validation 2h, 10% canary afterward.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell the customer: temporary sanitizer + pricing note, hotfix plan and ETA, and ask them to share the full raw request and any more X-Request-Ids. Scheduling a 30-min call to walk through. :thumbsup:
